utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand the parties have --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. One is more of a housekeeping issue. We have an outstanding motion to compel disclosure which the OTP did not file a response. It's namely in relation to the Koric killing or the Koric killing count whereof only one witness has testified so far on that case. The motion to compel is simply that we received an earlier redacted statement of which the motion to compel is based on. That appears to have an eyewitness where the name of the witness has been redacted and the witness saw someone else shoot Ms. Koric. That's important because on just Friday's disclosures in that batch where, according to the OTP index, it appears we received a document from the same person. Again, the name is redacted, and in order for us to do investigation on the Koric killing, of course, that would be some pertinent information to have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could deal with that at the first break, I'll have someone look into the it. I'm not intimately familiar with the matter that Mr. Alarid is speaking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. First break, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And secondarily to that, Your Honour, is simply that with Witness VG-142, Mr. Milan Lukic, and we filed a motion with that copying the Court, would like to ask pertinent questions regarding his detention with this witness. He's been advised of the potential pitfalls present in such an endeavour, including the risk of, in fact, technically testifying through his own questioning; however, the client is insistent considering the nature of this witness. However, I would like an opportunity to reserve cross-examination should the client wish my assistance, and I would like an opportunity to voir dire the witness as to relevance, similar to the instance where I moved to strike the witness based on not being relevant to the alibi. I think this witness also potentially is not particularly relevant to the alibi rebuttal considering the fact that he was not questioned on -- regarding any of the actual days in question in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I am not myself aware of the motion of which you speak. When was it filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It was submitted yesterday, Your Honour, last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he's to testify this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And why so late?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Basically, making the decision with the client, we talked to him on Monday -- I mean, excuse me, Friday. I've been trying to dissuade him, of course, because I think, you know, in the grand scheme of things, it's always a risk when the client does the interview. But he has a working knowledge of the circumstances --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The interview of my client in October of 1992. I mean, it is -- it is him being present at this interview that is the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you can raise that matter when the time comes for cross-examination, so we'll not rule on it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no preliminary matters. I'm ready to call witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, did you have any matters to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Just related to VG-142, and just for the record, we received, related to disclosure material, we just received yesterday additional document related to this witness. Actually, this witness is not related to our case because this is a rebuttal witness related to Milan Lukic's alibi. But I would like to stress this thing, that this disclosure material we received very, very late. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the documents that I was going to put to this witness is a document that was -- the Chamber, in a decision over the summer, granted the Prosecution leave to add to its exhibit list. That has been disclosed, and I'm not sure of the exact date, but it was disclosed shortly after we received it. Yesterday, when I was scheduled to meet with the witness, the witness informed VWS that he had no wish to meet with anyone from the Prosecution. So, therefore, I have to lay a foundation for this document. So the document Mr. Cepic, I believe, is referring to is the transmittal letter from the government of Serbia when it gave us this document. That's all it is, and it will only be used to set the foundation for the document itself which was already determined could be added to the exhibit list by the Chamber. So it's simply because of the circumstances, and it's a letter which simply says that this -- this document has been provided by the government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, but, nonetheless, every effort must be made to ensure that the other party has relevant documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the record is clear, I was notified about 2.30 yesterday evening that the witness was refusing to speak with me because he would have been able to authenticate it and it would have been no problem. Before 3.00 -- and Mr. Cepic might perhaps check his e-mail, but it was around 3.00 that I sent the material. So I tried to respond to the situation as it developed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, and just for the record, this document is from the January of 2008. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, then, Your Honour, I must say that's a document that's been disclosed quite some time ago, and I will get the date of exactly when that document was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness be brought in. Mr. Groome, I am reminded that the decision that the Trial Chamber issued regarding this witness indicated that examination-in-chief should be limited to five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I did want to ask for a variance of that. But before I do that, Your Honour, the court officer wasn't here last week when you ordered facial distortion for the witness, so I wanted to make sure of that before he is brought in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: All protective measures are in place, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to ask for a variance of that order which you issued on the 29th of August, and ask for the customary half hour with the 92 ter witness. There are a few exhibits that I -- a statement of Mr. Lukic and some other things that I don't believe I can put it to him in five minutes. But I don't expect that I would be more than 30 minutes, so I would ask leave of the Court to proceed briefly as possible through his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Groome, half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-142, last weekend, in accordance with a request from your government, the Trial Chamber issued an order directing that you receive certain protective measures for your testimony here today. They include the concealment of your name, your face, and your former position. This will be accomplished by referring to you during the course of your testimony as "VG-142," as well as distorting the image of your face in the public broadcast of these proceedings. The Chamber will direct, where appropriate, that portions of your testimony which compromise your identity or your work be conducted in private sessions that are not broadcast to the public. I'd ask you to, at this stage, take a look at a piece of paper, and it's a pseudonym sheet. I'd ask you to take a look at the piece of paper that the court officer -- or the court usher has given you. Is that your name on the piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that your correct date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, after the Defence and the Chamber has had an opportunity to see that sheet of paper, I would tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to sign the sheet of paper before it's shown to Defence and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the pseudonym sheet will become Exhibit number 143, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-142, I want to draw your attention to the 20th of June, 2008, and the 3rd of July, 2008, and ask you whether you gave a statement to investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: This copy I have with me, you mean? I have a copy of the statement with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement on those dates that I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The copy -- the copy is still in possession of usher, so it would be easier if we wait just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It seems that he has his own copy as well, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there an interpreter present to facilitate communication between yourself and the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the statement translated into your own language for you to read before you confirmed it with your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is your statement an accurate account of the information that you provided to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphones, thank you, or speak up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you're being asked to come closer to the microphone. Perhaps the usher could assist. The interpreter is having some difficulty hearing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would ask a copy of that statement be placed on the e-court screen. It is ERN number 0635-8438.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there's two television screens in front of you. The one to the right will be used to display different documents to you during the course of your examination. Can I ask you to look at the screen on the right, and, momentarily, you should see the first page of that statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that the first page of the statement that you gave in June and July of this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that we now go to page 6 of the original document and to the signature block at the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at page 6 now of that document. Is that your signature contained on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you give honest and truthful answers in this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And now that you have been sworn in as a witness, if you were to ask -- if I were to ask you the same questions, would you give the same responses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there anything about your statement that you wish to change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I wouldn't change anything, except perhaps in paragraph 18, that my only involvement in the work of the section for suppressing extremism and terrorism was the interview with Milan Lukic and the interview -- or, rather, conversation next day I had with my colleague concerning Milan Lukic. It is perhaps a bit vague in the statement, but I believe the sentence included in the statement does reflect it and does confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We've noted that amendment now to your statement. Is there anything else you'd like to change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, the Prosecution tenders the statement of VG-142, that's ERN 0635-8438, as a Prosecution exhibit, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P144, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, neither this witness nor the government of Serbia have specifically requested protective measures regarding this had statement. I believe that this is an oversight. It would be consistent with the other protective measures ordered by the Chamber with respect to the testimony of this witness and the underlying documents that any public version of his statement have the same information regarding his identity, the name of the of victim, and the people who his report was sent to redacted. I have done this in an additional statement, and at this time would tender a redacted version of his statement as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P145, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-142, you have just told us in private session which organisation of the Serbian government you worked. I want to now draw your attention to the 26th of October, 1992. During the course of engaging in your lawful duties, did you become aware that a person by the name of Milan Lukic had been detained?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to avoid any -- any doubt later on, I think that we have some mistakes in the statement. Actually, in paragraph 17, the witness quoted: "I have been shown a document entitled "Centar of DB Uzice," and numbers 79047 and 79043. Firstly, we could not find that material either in e-court or disclosure material; and, secondly, the witness in paragraph 18 explains a completely different document under the number 79047. So it could be mistake related to paragraph 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We note the points you have raised, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-142, if we could return to my question about whether on the 26th of October, 1992, you became aware that a person by the name of Milan Lukic had been arrested or detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, were you aware.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where he was when he was detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: From the supervisor of my own section, I learnt that I should come to the centre to interview a certain person. My supervise didn't tell me over the phone who it was. I arrived at the centre; and in the meantime, Milan Lukic, who had been detained, or rather, arrested at the border creasing called Uvac between Bosnia and Serbia, was brought into custody together with another man, his fellow fighter --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could ask you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: -- to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the other person that he was taken into custody with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I know the name is Dragicevic. I don't remember the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic in possession of any weapons at the time of his arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: That is precisely the reason why he was of taken into custody and brought in. He was found to have weapons, and it was not allowed to move around with weapons in the territory of the Republic of Serbia. He was in uniform and so was his fellow fighter, so that's the reason why he was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you file a record of interview that included a list of weapons he was in possession of at the time he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: That's reflected in my Official Note, the original document that I drafted after the interview.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: What was found on Milan Lukic and his fellow fighter when they were arrested and brought in --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: -- I found out that from --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Please finish your sentence. I'm sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I was informed about that by the member of the Secretariat of Internal Affairs who had detained him and brought him to Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll be tendering your report in a few minutes and the Chamber will have a full list of those weapons. The question I want too ask you now is rather limited: Are you familiar with weapons that could be properly characterised as sniper rifles?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is outside the scope of an alibi rebuttal. I mean, the bottom line is, Your Honour, this witness has testified on a blanket argument that because he was interviewed in October of 1992 and questioned about something that the interviewer knew occurred on June 20th, 1992, yet is caught with weapons in October of 1992. It's not relevant to what weapons he has, nor does it go to the basis of alibi rebuttal; and, in fact, Your Honour, I'd like an opportunity to voir dire the witness because I think the entire testimony is not relevant to alibi rebuttal despite the proffer of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where do you think you are, what state?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to the issue of this witness, that's already been resolved. With respect to the sniper rifle, many of the witnesses have included descriptions of the weapons as part of their description, and the alibi is that they have their own person. So it is highly relevant to the alibi whether or not, at the time of his arrest, he had a weapon that matched the description given by witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: An alibi goes to a date and time, not what someone had in their possession three months later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're going to allow the question, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have a very narrow view of what constitutes an alibi and what constitutes alibi rebuttal evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am sorry. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like an opportunity to voir dire the witness in terms of his questioning of my client without the right of counsel on charges that include high crimes and felonies, i.e., murder and kidnapping, and he did this without counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: With a view to what? With a view to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You're going to introduce technically what amounts to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What I want to find out is you want to ask questions in a voir dire now, or in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I mean, in a bench trial scenario, Your Honour, I understand the Judges can normally differentiate; but in a jury trial situation, of course, I would normally want to exclude the witness prior to hearing the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. You can ask whatever you wish to ask when your time for cross-examination comes, and it will then be for the Trial Chamber to determine the propriety of the questions. Mr. Groome, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can I remind you of the question that I've put to you: Are you familiar with weapons that could be properly characterised as sniper rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I had the occasion to see it, but I have to emphasise that I am -- I haven't seen Milan Lukic carrying any weapon. He was brought onto the premises of the service in Uzice to be questioned. His arrest, when he was found wearing a uniform and carrying a weapon, happened at the border crossing 70 kilometres away. It was done by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, VG-142, in the weapons that you list in your report, are any of those weapons that could be properly characterised as a sniper's rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: You mean the weapons listed in my Official Note?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. Could any of those, to your knowledge, be characterise the as a sniper's rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: From what I know, none of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you why he was -- why he was detained. Your government has requested that the name of the victim not be mentioned in open court. Could I ask you to refer to the name of the victim as simply "Mr. P," and not use his full name. Why was Mr. Lukic detained?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've referred to some documents that he had on him at the time of his arrest. What documents did he have on him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance. It doesn't go to alibi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the -- the Court a few weeks ago asked me what happened -- ultimately happened to the red Passat. One of the documents that was recovered from this witness was the registration document in the name of Lukic, Mile Lukic, to that car. All of this is very relevant to the alibi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what documents were on Mr. Lukic at the time of his arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears that the witness is reading his statement from the bench. We would ask that he exhaust his own recollection before refreshing his recollection with the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, are you, in fact, referring to your statement before answering the questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm jogging my memory. You must keep one thing in mind, this was 16 years ago. What I remember now about the events is far less than is reflected in the statement. I'm being perfectly honest about this, and that's what I told the investigators, too, when I spoke to them. This was, after all, 16 years ago, and this was merely one of many interviews that I conducted throughout my career; and, believe me, there have quite name of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps, VG-142, if you need to refresh your memory, please just ask the Court for permission to look at your original report, and the Court will decide whether you're able to do that. So do you need to look at your original report to refresh your memory as to the documents that were taken from or found on Mr. Lukic at the time of his arrest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you need to look at your report, at your statement, then ask us. Let us know, and we will tell you whether you can. There is nothing intrinsically wrong, inherently wrong with your looking at the statement. It will be a matter for the Chamber to determine what weight to attach to your evidence in light of that fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I please have a look?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I please have a look just to jog my memory to see what he had on him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is your memory refreshed as to the documents that were --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the documents were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: He had ID bearing the name of "Popovic, Njegos," "Njegos Popovic," and a driver's licence bearing the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any other documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Based on what I was told, there was the vehicle registration document as well that he was found with, and, apparently, that was in his father's name, purportedly the real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that 65 ter number 192 be placed on the screen for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, momentarily, you'll see an image on the screen to your right. I'd ask you to look at the screen and tell us whether or not you recognise the documents on the screen. Sir, do you recognise what's depicted on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is depicted on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: This is the ID, the driver's licence, and the vehicle registration document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that the court officer zoom in on one of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The photograph that we're looking at, is this somehow attached to the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Which document? There's three referenced: An identification, a driver's licence, and a registration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, the document that we're looking at now on the screen, the picture to the left -- well, let me ask you more broadly. Were there photographs attached to any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: At the time, each of these documents had a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And there appears to be a circle on the corners of the photographs. Can you tell us - we don't have the originals here - what are those circles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: These circles are small metal rings used to bind the different pages of these documents together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would tender 65 ter number 192 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P146, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, if all of his identification documents were in the name of Popovic, Njegos, how did you know that his true name was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Milan Lukic was brought to the Uzice police station, the Uzice SUP, as Milan Lukic, because the employees of the Priboj SUP who had detained him recognised him to be Milan Lukic. They also realised that the documents he was carrying were forged, that he was using forged documents. As soon as he arrived in Uzice, which is where I was working at the time, where my unit was working, he was already a person whose identity had been by this time established.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you've used the term "Priboj SUP." Could you please tell us precisely what is SUP, S-U-P?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The Secretariat of Internal Affairs, the Uzice branch. This is a branch of the Ministry of Interior of Serbia, and it covers a number of municipalities including Priboj. The Priboj police station is also included. This is a branch of the Ministry of Interior, the one based in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Milan Lukic was interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: When exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After his arrest.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: An interview had been conducted with him at the station in Priboj when he was brought in, and then he was taken through to the Uzice SUP where he was ID'd by employees of the Uzice SUP. After that, my own unit was involved, and Milan Lukic was brought to our building, to our premises where we interviewed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you personally interviewed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes. I personally interviewed him on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've testified earlier that he was arrested in the company of another person. Was the -- was your interview of him conducted with just him or with both of the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The two were separated. Milan Lukic was brought to a room where I was with my team, and then he was interviewed; whereas, his fellow fighter, the person he had been detained in the company of, was taken to a different room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did the entire interview that you conducted take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The interview was commenced at 2300 hours and was completed at 9.00 the following morning; 11.00 in the evening on the 26th and the completion occurred on the 27th at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the interview conducted in compliance with any applicable laws of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why is that leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It suggests the answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe if it was leading, it would have a "weren't they." Again, this is my first opportunity ever to speak with this man. I'm simply asking him did he conduct it in appliance with applicable laws in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, was -- was the interview conducted in compliance with Serbian law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Absolutely. This was an official interview; and the interview, the way it was conducted, conformed with all the norms and rules that applied at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was any force --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: There was every indication that he had been involved in -- absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any force or other coercive methods used during the interview by yourself or anyone else who was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Certainly not. Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the interview recorded in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The interview was recorded at the time. I had received orders from my superior to do that. This was very common course of action in situations such as these. Interviews would be taped when one didn't know exactly how they would go. The purpose of this, the primary purpose being to draft a document based on the tape recording. These documents are kept for up to a month and then destroyed, the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you create any written notes or written record of the interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It was precisely based on this interview that was recorded in its entirety that I drew up a summary, and the result of this is the document that I now have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before I -- or could I ask that that document, that 65 ter number 35, be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While that is being done, do you know if the audiotape of the interview is still in existence today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, it was destroyed. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know anything about the circumstances under which it was destroyed, such as when and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, I don't, but this was very common. Interviews that were taped in this way left tapes behind; but then a month later, these tapes would be destroyed or reused for taping a different interview. That was just the done thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, 65 ter number 35 is now up on the screen before you. I'd ask you to take a look at it and ask you: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I see that I was the person who authored this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you that we go to the -- to the last page of -- of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could just move down a little bit. Your Honour, there is a bit of a delay. There are two versions of each of these documents, a redacted version -- one redacted in clients with the Chamber's order of the 18th of September, and one unredacted. For each of these documents, I will be tendering the unredacted, under seal, and then the redacted version as a public exhibit. The wrong document was picked up. I see again we have the redacted one. If we could have 65 ter number 35, it's the unredacted one where the witness will be able to view his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at what's on the bottom of the screen now. Do you recognise the signature --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Just a minute, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Da [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I believe the Chamber didn't hear your last answer. Do you recognise the sit on the bottom of the page on the screen before us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this the document that you created at the time or shortly after you conducted the interview of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes. That is the document that I produced following my interview with Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I would tender 65 ter number 35, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit P147, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you have gone well beyond now the 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there have been a number of objections. I hope the Court doesn't think I've wasted any time, but I'm moving as expeditiously through what I believe is extraordinarily important evidence. There have been a number of objections, and I'd also ask the Chamber to keep in mind that the witness declined to speak with me. So it would have been much more efficient if I would have been able to give him these documents and ask him to review them yesterday, but I just did not have that ability. I respected his wishes. So that's some of the delay, but I assure the Chamber I will move an expeditiously as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Lets move on as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would tender 65 ter number 35.1 as a public exhibit. It is a derivative exhibit. It is 65 ter number 35, now P147, with redactions made to the document in compliance with the Trial Chamber's order of the 18th of September, 2008. The order required redactions of the name of the victim, the name of VG-142, and the offices to which the document was sent after VG-142 drafted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number P148.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask now that 65 ter number 191 be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at this document on the screen and ask you whether or not you recognise it. This is 65 ter number 191.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I recognise this document. This was a component part of the Official Note that I submitted. The document, however, was physically produced by an employee of the Uzice SUP because that was that person's job, the reason being the document has to do with the investigation looking into the murder of P.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that the witness be shown the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there's a signature at the bottom of that page. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Milan Lukic's signature, at least as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter number 191 into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we would object for the record, Your Honour, as lack of foundation. He didn't indicate that the signature was, in fact, Milan Lukic the accused here. That's never been established, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can ask a follow-up question if the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, have you -- were you aware of any other person by the name of "Milan Lukic" that had been implicated in either the death of Mr. P or the kidnapping of the people from Sjeverin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was this statement signed of Milan Lukic, was it submitted with your original note of your interview of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes. I got this from the -- an inspector in the Uzice SUP, and it was attached to my note.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd renew my tender of this exhibit of 65 ter number 191.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would renew my objection, lack of foundation, as the document was not signed in front of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number P149, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, today, I've been dealing just with technical issues. Just for clarification, this document is -- has got 65 ter number 191.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that may be some confusion. I think I know what the source of the confusion is. We received the original from Serbia partially redacted. So the version that should be up there now is 191, which would only have the redactions that we received from the government of Serbia. The next document I was going to tender was 191.1, which has an additional redaction in order to make it comply with the Chamber's order of the 18th of September, 2008, and I think there was one other mention of the victim's name. So I'm at this time tendering 191 as a document -- or an exhibit, under seal, and 191.1 fully redacted as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just as a technical issue, yesterday, I spoke to Mr. Van Hooydonk at 4.00 p.m., and he informed me that -- that there is no document 191 in the system. I requested that document unredacted, and I was informed that just redacted form existing in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can we get to the bottom of this and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Simply, I think my explanation covered that. We did not receive a fully unredacted version from Serbia. What Serbia sent us, and the only copy we have, was partially redacted. There was some information removed and, as you can see, some blacking out on the document. In order to comply with the Chamber's order, the victim's name was mentioned, and even the Chamber when it admitted the document brought out that fact -- or I'm sorry. When the Chamber issued its order in response to Serbia's motion for protective measures, the Chamber had noted that the document had already come with substantial redactions. 191.1 is simply the redacted document that we received from Serbia, plus an additional redaction, to fully comply with the army's order of the 18th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, move on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 191 will become Exhibit number P149, under seal; and 65 ter number 191.1 will become Exhibit number P150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting, but we haven't got the document 191 in the system. I'm little bit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask the court deputy to clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could I please ask the counsel to switch off the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 191 is now on the screen, but it's not been broadcasted since it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I'll ask the court deputy on the break to bring you up-to-date. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: An important matter brought to me by Mr. Ivetic is, if you note in the last paragraph of the English version, it says -- on that second to last paragraph, actually, that in reference to the weapons, it says: "... that were taken from me, specifically." But Mr. Ivetic noted in the B/C/S version, it says: "... taken from him." That is an indication that this was not a statement of Mr. Milan Lukic, but a statement written by someone else, unless Mr. Lukic refers to himself in the third person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's a matter for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's a point to raise in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It just represents an error in the translation of the document submitted by the -- not so much an error in the statement itself in B/C/S, but an error in the translation of the English version which would be before the Court. Of course, this gentleman couldn't be cross-examined on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to translation errors, I'm happy to have it resubmitted to CLSS, if the Chamber feels that's warranted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I would like now to return to the record of the interview of Milan Lukic, now in evidence as P148. Without telling us the information that you provided, my question to you is simply: Did he provide information about his date of birth, his parents' names, and other biographical information that you duly recorded in your record of interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would now like to show you an excerpt of your Official Note, which is now in evidence as P148, and seek your comment. I would like to draw your attention to the second page of the B/C/S original, the third paragraph from the top, and the 17th line of that paragraph, and the usher will assist you by focusing in on at that section. The original begins with the words, "Po zavrsetku..." In English translation, it is also the second page, third new paragraph, on line 15 of that paragraph and states: "When the training was completed, we went to Visegrad where we placed ourselves under the command of the Visegrad SUP as part of the Visegrad TO. Together with my unit, I participated in all important military operations in the Visegrad area. This is a real inter-ethnic war, and I came to the front with only one goal, to protect Serbs and Serbdom in this area." What does the phrase "Visegrad SUP" stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I assume this is the secretariat of Interior -- of Internal Affairs in Visegrad which was BH territory back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would local police in Visegrad also be part of the Visegrad SUP, S-U-P?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation, and he's not been tendered as an expert in the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to provide that information, Witness; and, if so, give us the basis for your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you this, in the interview with Milan Lukic I noted exactly what he said: "We placed ourselves under the command of SUP Visegrad as part of the Territorial Defence." That's what he said, and that's what I noted it -- how I noted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The question for you is now -- that is now before you is: Are you able to see whether or not police in Visegrad would also have been considered part of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: In my view, it's the same, the police and the SUP. I don't know, that's the way I interpreted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My next question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why is that? Why are they the same? Tell us why.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Secretariat of Internal Affairs is an organisational unit of the Ministry of the Interior. I suppose the Secretariat of Internal Affairs comprises both the police and the civilians who work in that secretariat. I'm telling you following the logic that applies in Serbia where we live.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My next question to you is: Did at any time during the course of the interview did he say that this relationship with the Visegrad SUP had terminated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: As far as I remember, during the interview, he said that, being dissatisfied and disenchanted at one point, he left Visegrad and went to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recall if he tell you when he did that, when he left Visegrad for Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I can't recall that now. I can only look at my notes and try to remember, but it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention, once again, to the second page of the B/C/S original, just a couple of sentences after the last excerpt. The last sentence in the original begins with the words "Svojim licnim ..." In the English, this excerpt reads: "Setting a personal example, I had quite some influence on the readiness of Serbian soldiers, and I personally liquidate ..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. This is beyond the scope of alibi rebuttal. This has nothing to do with alibi rebuttal. This is attempting to bring in evidence unrelated to alibi rebuttal in through this witness improperly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document that is already in evidence, and I'm ... [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we're going to be moving to strike this document from evidence following cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understand the Defence case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, it is relevant, but is it part of alibi rebuttal? Explain to us how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this case, the Defence case of Milan Lukic, as I understand it, was that he was not present at the time when two large numbers of people were -- were killed, and I believe a term that would be used for such large exterminations would be "liquidated." It is the Prosecution's case that this controverts that assertion because it is an admission that he personally liquidated many Muslims. It's clearly directly on point or counters his assertion here in this trial that he did not do that because he was not present to be able to do that. Now, it's certainly up to Mr. Alarid or Mr. Lukic to say in their case that his reference to "I personally liquidated many Muslims" either wasn't said or refers to an other group of people. But it is certainly the Prosecution's case that this is a direct reference to the large number of people that were placed in houses and set on fire in Pionirska Street and in Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that is reaching. To imply that this statement marks an admission by a party of culpability in these two house fires is outrageous. There is no reference to time, place, in anyway, shape, or form. In fact, this witness testified in the same note that, in fact, Mr. Lukic was being honest about being a soldier. What we do -- must concede here is this was a war zone and people were dying, and he refers specifically in this note, the witness, not Mr. Lukic, because the tapes of this were -- nine hours of tapes were destroyed in a murder investigation. That in and of itself is outrageous, regarding the fact that this was a murder investigation without statute of limitations, not some misdemeanour being investigated by the police. But the fact of the matter is that to imply that this in an alibi rebuttal situation somehow infers an absolute acquiescence to these crimes is outrageous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to finish reading that portion of the statement, and then I have a question that I want to -- to ask you. "So I personally liquidated many Muslims-extremists in the Visegrad area who were known to have maltreated the Serbian population. I am uncompromising in opposing Muslim soldiers. And in contrast to the Serbs from Visegrad, when I came there, I came ready to kill anyone who was threatening Serbdom. I dispensed with tolerance in advance and so did the whole group which I lead." In this passage, you recorded him as saying he personally liquidated many Muslims. Did you ask him any more detailed questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- about how meany people or under what circumstances this occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... if you would allow me to finish my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection to the mischaracterisation of the witness. It was specifically noted that there was a reference to extremists and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Alarid, the reference was to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Muslims -- well, Mr. Groome in his question, referred to Muslims, of course implying other than, I'm assuming, Muslim soldiers or extremists. But in the note itself, there's a specific reference to extremists and then soldiers. I would just ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You want us to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- on page 34, line 17 to 24, I read it, and in my reading of it, I use both the words that are in the translation, extremists --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: "I personally liquidated many Muslims-extremists ..." --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Speakers are kindly asked not to speak at the same time for the sake of the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... at the same time. Now let us be clear as to what exactly is in the statement. Is there a reference to Muslims as one category of persons who are liquidated, and extremists as another set?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the words "extremists" and "soldiers" are used. I said that when I read it, and I'll read that portion for the Chamber. "I personally liquidated many Muslims-extremists in the Visegrad area who were known to have maltreated the Serbian population. I am uncompromising in opposing Muslim soldiers," and it goes on. And if the Chamber looks back at my earlier reading of this passage, I've read it just as I've said it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So my question to you, sir: In this passage you, recorded him as saying he personally liquidated many Muslims. Did you ask him any more detailed questions about that, when, how many, any other questions to follow-up on that assertion by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: When he stated this in so many words, that he liquidated a great number of Muslim-extremists in the territory of Visegrad who were known to have been maltreating Serbian population, and he said exactly in those words that he was uncompromising and that he had dispensed with tolerance, I noted it down exactly in the same words that he used. And from his talk, I understood that he meant Muslim-extremists who had in some way mistreated the Serbs in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to the kidnapping, did he deny the kidnapping of the people from Sjeverin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance. This is an incident that occurred in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can explain the relevance, if the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, when Mr. Lukic denied to this witness that he had done Sjeverin, he said, but if he had, he would have done it in a certain way. I believe the way that he will describe will mirror the way in which the crimes at Pionirska Street and Bikavac were committed. So it goes to modus operandi, which is certainly evidence that the Chamber can use to ascertain the identity of the person who committed these crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then this witness should have been listed as a witness in chief, not as an alibi rebuttal witness. The pathway for this is improper, and also highly speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are not allowing that question. You are going too far with the questioning of this witness, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He's here for alibi rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit number 150. Can I ask the court officer to go to the first page of both statements, and focus on the first paragraph under the heading of "Statement." It reads: "I have been under on the front in Visegrad and its surroundings since the 10th of April, 1992. I am the commander of a group called the Avenger, initially known as the Obrenovac Detachment. The group has between 20 and 50 men, and is under the command of the Visegrad TO and I am directly subordinate to Vinko Pandurevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question to you, VG-142, is: In the course of your duties, as you've described to the Chamber in closed session, what information do you know about the activities of this group of men from Obrenovac Serbia, who call themselves the Avengers?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. It calls for speculation and well beyond the scope of an alibi rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, in the course of your duties, do you have any -- any knowledge about this group that call themselves the Avengers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I told you, at the beginning, that I was involved in this interview with Milan Lukic, together with my interviewing team; and this statement that Milan Lukic made was given to the crime inspector. This statement is an attachment to the Official Note that I drafted. At that time, it was not my field of expertise. It was not my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I'll ask you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I was involved in the interview because I was appointed as part of that interviewing team.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the passage that I read you, it records Milan Lukic as saying he was in Visegrad since the 10th of April, 1992. During the course of the lengthy interview that you conducted with him, did he tell you what periods of time he was not present in Visegrad; and, if so, would you please enumerate them for us here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: From what I know, he arrived in Visegrad in April and stayed there until September, I believe. I cannot clearly remember this Official Note at this point, but it's in the Official Note the way it was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I now like to draw your attention to the second paragraph of the B/C/S original. In the eighth line of that statement, a sentence begins with "Ne secam se koji ..." In the translation, it is the last sentence on the page and continues to the second page, and I'll read it: "While we were passing by the -- by, I gave them a signal to follow the column because I was with Sasa and Gordana in a red Passat, which I owned actually. It was registered in my father's name, and a column of cars from my group drove behind me." Do you know if the red Passat that Milan Lukic is referring to in this statement is the same car he was arrested in?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation and beyond the scope of alibi. How could this witness testify as to the exact car stopped in -- that supposedly is referenced in the statement, without reference to a licence plate or VIN number, all the way to a car that he stopped in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm simply asking whether he knows, Your Honour. If he says that he doesn't, then I'm obviously limited in what I can ask him. But I simply asking does he know whether the red Passat referred to was the one he was arrested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to answer the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see that car. The only thing I can say, and that corresponds to what I learnt in my interview with Milan Lukic, is that it was a red Passat vehicle registered to his father's name. Whether it's the same car, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask that Prosecution Exhibit 146 be placed on the screen. This is -- one of the documents on P146 is the registration that was recovered from Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, VG-142, when I -- when you can see this, I would ask you to tell us what is the model -- what is the make and model of the car for which this registration is for? If you need to focus in on or have the court officer zoom in on a particular piece, please just indicate which portion of the screen you'd like enlarged.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It's a passenger vehicle, Passat, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the model year of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: According to this document, I believe the year of production is 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does the registration --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It keeps shifting on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does the registration indicate the year in which the car was first registered? Again, if you need us to move the document, that can be done.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It cannot be seen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that we scroll down to see the entire document, and if we could zoom in on the upper left-hand corner of the image that we see now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to this, the year of production is 1990; but I see from the document, it says "brown."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So does it indicate the colour of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: "Chassis number, brown metallic," it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does it indicate the year that it was first registered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: You know, this part is not visible on the screen. It's precisely where the information on first registration is: 19 -- I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you're -- a copy of the documents that you produced in 1992, that was provided for you at the beginning of your testimony. I believe it also includes a copy of this document. So, if you're better able to see a hard copy in front you, I believe you have that in front of you. Who is listed as the owner on the registration certificate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: You have to move to the vehicle registration paper. The owner is stated as Lukic Mile.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the last thing I want to ask you about Prosecution Exhibit 150 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could please move back to P150.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This time I'd like to ask you to look at a section. The first page, the second paragraph of the B/C/S original, this time line 17, beginning with the words, in Serbian, "Od Lukic Sredoje." In the English translation, it appears on the second page and is six lines line from the top of the page. It states: "I learned from Sredoje Lukic, a relative of mine, and from the police at the check-point at Mokra Gora, that," and here the redaction of the name of the victim," Mokra Gora that was caught with the Muslims whom he was taking for money or just like that over to Serbia. The police discovered him, he was tied with them to fence by the Uzice police, and on that day, he was taken to the Uzice SUP." My question to you is: In the course of investigating the events that you were involved in, was there any investigation conducted to determine whether Sredoje Lukic was involved --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Finish the question, but don't answer, because Mr. Cepic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any investigation, that you know of, of Sredoje Lukic in connection with the events surrounding the death of Mr. P?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cepic, what's your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not a witness related to our case, and I read very carefully notification actually submission for this witness. My client is not mentioned anywhere, never mind if the witness can answer on that. I do not object. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, Mr. Cepic. If the witness can answer, he will answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, we would object that it's simply outside the scope of the alibi rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we note that. Answer, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any investigation conducted into whether or not Sredoje Lukic was involved in circumstances surrounding the death of Mr. P, the person we're referring to as Mr. P?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I have to emphasise, once again, this is a statement that Milan Lukic gave to the crime inspector regarding the circumstances of the death of Mr. P. In my interview with Milan Lukic, we never touched upon Sredoje Lukic, nor was he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've told us, in your testimony, about Milan Lukic being arrested on suspicion of several different crimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we're well beyond the time now for the break. How much more time would you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have three more questions, Your Honour. I have three more questions, but they require showing an exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, to wrap up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified about the arrest of Milan Lukic. Do you have -- do you know how long he was held in custody; or if he was released, when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Following the interview at the Uzice HQ, Milan Lukic was detained for the next 48 hours, and this is something that was imposed by the public prosecutor. I have no idea what became of Milan Lukic later on. I later did nothing whatsoever in the line of work that had to could with Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you ever called to testify at a hearing or a trial related to your work on this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, for my last question, I'd ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-142, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Mr. Alarid. Now, before you begin, Mr. Alarid, during examination-in-chief, you had objected to the admission of statements made by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And your main argument, your general argument, if I understood you correctly, was that those statements were obtained by methods which would cast some doubt on their reliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, normally, also, you know, addressing the rights of counsel during an accused's questioning on such a serious matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, these are matters that you will raise in cross-examination with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was, although my client still wishes to do the factual portion of the cross-examination. My focus would be on the procedural issues of which might sway the Court into not accepting this

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to be sure. You will cross-examine on this, because what I intend to do is that in relation to those statements that I had admitted, I'm going to revise the ruling so that they are marked for identification instead of admitted. Then at the end of your cross-examination, we'll make a determination on their admissibility. So I'll ask the court deputy to take note of that, that those statements are marked for identification pending the cross-examination by counsel. So you may begin, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I apologise, Your Honour. I brought up Mr. P's name in public session. We will need to do a redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The court deputy will bring that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And has the Court made a decision on Mr. Lukic beginning the cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are your arguments?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the arguments is that, quite frankly, he knows the facts much better relating his being in custody at the time. That's why I'm saying for the factual portion, clearly Mr. Lukic has the advantage. Making the legal arguments, I think, obviously I'd like to handle that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the basic jurisprudential ground on which you're relying, because my understanding is that where an accused is represented by counsel, then it is counsel who does the questioning, and I'd like you to show me that that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we referenced in our motion extensively the Prlic et al. trial, which has allowed a limited or qualified self-representation, despite the assignment of counsel. In this particular case, we would simply ask that Mr. Lukic be afforded the same courtesies and rights under the Tribunal to question this witness based on his superior knowledge of the facts and circumstances of the case, as well as definitely the facts and circumstances of this detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... understanding, and we have looked at that case from the Appeals Chamber, which makes it quite clear that when an accused is effectively represented by counsel, it is in principle for the counsel to conduct the examination of witnesses. Of course, it does go on to identify some exceptional circumstances in which an accused may be authorised to participate in the examination in person. In the Chamber's view, those exceptional circumstances do not apply here, and we will not allow questioning by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then all I would ask, Your Honour, is to reserve the possibility of recalling the witness on the defence pending maybe a revisiting of the issue, but I understand the Court's ruling today and respect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, your mic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you meant by recalling the witness. We have, in fact, ruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. VG-142, good morning. My name is Jason Alarid, and I represent Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that the only contact you had with Mr. Lukic was during this nine hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, this was the only time in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this was in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the exact date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The 26th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that, in fact, Mr. Lukic was arrested on the 27th of October, 1992, and stayed in custody until November 4th 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Milan Lukic was arrested on the 26th at the Uvac border crossing by the Priboj police. He was then taken to Uzice. That same day -- that after noon, rather, or early that evening, I was informed an hour before I was supposed to interview him that he was on his way there. The interview commenced at exactly 2300 hours on the 26th and was completed at 9.00 in the morning the following day, the 27th.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all the other microphones not being used please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so -- but you indicated he was questioned earlier, and that's where the statement regarding Mr. P was generated; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, no, no. That is in error. Milan Lukic may have been questioned while he was at the Priboj police station; nevertheless, the statement was produced, I believe, on the 27th. It was towards the end of our interview. The inspector interviewed Milan Lukic about the circumstances surrounding the murder of P; and then as a result of that interview, a statement was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you have evidence that Mr. Lukic was processed in the Priboj SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The evidence, for me, was that he had been brought there as Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But do you have evidence that he had been processed, that he had been formally arrested, that proper documents had been generated, and that he had been interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: At the time he was brought in -- at the time he was brought to the office in which I talked to him, he was brought there by a uniformed police officer and a crime inspector in plain clothes. The inspector attended some portions of the interview as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was this inspector that generated the statement, not yourself; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Correct, yes, and that's precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, in fact, you left the room at certain times, leaving Mr. Lukic alone with this other inspector; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Correct, in principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, in fact, it wasn't your goal to make any questions related to June of 1992. Your focus was on October of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. The murder of P is something for the crime police, and it certainly was not part of our work. When I say "our work," I mean the institution that I was working for.
