utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, in fact, questions may have been asked of the witness related to other times, but you wouldn't have had reason to ask them because your focus was on October; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but isn't it true that Milan Lukic was actually arrested at Sjeverin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I was told that he had been arrested at this border crossing and was carrying weapons at the time. This is something that was stated in the Official Note, and this was given as the reason for his detention, him being found there with weapons on him. Later, it was also established that he was carrying false documents, false ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you wouldn't have -- you have no information that Mr. Lukic was read and advised of his rights to counsel, do you, regarding the murder of Mr. P?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No information, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, in fact, nowhere in your Official Note do you reference a formal advice of rights of Mr. Lukic regarding the kidnapping of October; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, the interview was about facts -- or rather, indicia that he had been involved in a kidnapping, in a murder. Information was used that had been obtained from the police by this time, but these were all indicia at the time. He wasn't advised of his rights. The moment of his detention and him being brought into custody was simply taken advantage of in order to interview him about these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, he was not free to leave, correct, he was under arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: When he came to my office, when he was brought to my office, he was wearing a uniform and was, as a matter of fact, handcuffed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so he was not free to leave at any point in time during your investigation and contact with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he was, in fact, detained for longer than your interview, for 48 hours after you completed your interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The day he was brought from Priboj to Uzice, he was also brought to my office. The interview went on between 2300 hours the previous evening and 9.00 the following morning, and then the police took over again, the Uzice secretariat, the Uzice SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, again, during those nine hours, how much time of the time were you actually out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, you know, it was, for the most part, me and another colleague. We interviewed him together, and then one of us would leave the room occasionally; one at a time, I mean. But, for the most part, we remained in that room throughout the period that I specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you had the benefit of the tape recording. I'm assuming that's why you didn't mind leaving for periods of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet, under what authority does a potential recording that might be potential evidence in a murder investigation fall under a destruction order of 30 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, that tape could not be used as evidence, not even back then. I pointed out, at the outset, that the recording was used for the sole purpose of producing the primary document which was a result of that interview. You are entering an interview, the progress of which is uncertain simply because there is a lack of facts. So this is what you do in a situation like that; you tape the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true, though, that Mr. Lukic did not want to talk to you? He, in fact, refused to speak to you for a good portion of that nine hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: That is certainly true. Lukic, during that interview, adopted a restrictive approach. The interview took a long time, and we went back several times during the interview to his arrival, how he had come to be in the Visegrad area, and so on and so forth, in order to create more room for dialogue. He was quite reserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet, at what time had he been formally arrested before your first contact with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Lukic was officially detained and taken to the Priboj police station on the 26th, that morning, I assume; but I don't know the exact time. It was that afternoon that he was taken to Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And your first contact was at 11.00 p.m., one hour before midnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you interrogated him through the night, not allowing him to sleep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that that is a more aggressive form of interrogation, not allowing an individual to sleep, interviewing them through the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, this is operative work, especially when you have a case like this. This is something that was very much in the public eye, because these kidnappings were being noticed and were drawing a lot of attention. Milan Lukic appeared to have been involved, and this is the sort of handling that was required. We used the opportunity to interview him because he had been brought in as he had been found in the possession of illegal weapons and false ID. This was a unique opportunity to interview the man because of all the indicia previously arisen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you normally interview people through the night, not allowing them to sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The practice allowed that, too, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it something you had done before? Is it a practice you yourself had engaged in before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, this was a very particular situation. I know it's exhausting, but the situation made it an imperative to conduct this interview. I got an order from my supervisor to -- to carry out that interview, and I had to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that Mr. Lukic refused to speak and requested the military and police commander from Visegrad to attend this questioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're saying at no time did he request his commander to come from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: How would I have been able to secure the arrival of his commander from Visegrad to Uzice?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long of a drive is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Ninety kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long would it take you to drive that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a problem? It appears as if the witness did not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long would it take to drive that distance of 90 kilometres from the Uzice SUP to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: An hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So why not, if he's requesting his commander, why not just make that happen either by other means of communication, telephone or radio, or, in fact, just driving to get him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: That's the territory of another state.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But would it be fair to say that at the time the two states -- the Serbian forces in at that state were acting in cooperation with forces in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's the concern of the Serbian government that information about his actual tasks and title and affiliations be done in private session, so as not to compromise him and colleagues. So I'd ask that be redacted and any other biographical information perhaps can be done in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will reacted. And if you're going to follow that line, then we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are going to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the work of the RDB was strictly governed by the constitution of Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was followed by the Law on Internal Affairs; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And also governed by the Rule Book of State Security Services; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It was in conformity with the rules of the State Security Service as part of the state security sector of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that the main role of the RDB, as foreseen by those earlier documents we just talked about and foregoing instruments, was in relation to this investigation -- or was in relation to the investigation, arrest, and prevention of terrorism and crimes against the state of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It was a special part of the state security sector that dealt precisely with combatting extremism and terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, otherwise, isn't it true that the primary body in the MUP entrusted with the duty to investigate and apprehend perpetrators of actual criminal offences --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Alarid please slow down while reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- save offences of terrorism and against the state is the public security sector and not the RDB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Look, the kidnapping of 16 citizens of Sjeverin exceeded the importance of an ordinary kidnapping. Until that year, 1992, kidnapping was very rare in the territory of Serbia, and it was a traditional crime; but the kidnapping of 16 people made this a very high profile case. So the both the Public Security Service and the State Security Service received the assignment to investigate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who was your source regarding the investigation of the kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Alarid please also turn his microphone off when he's not using it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who was your confidential informant regarding any participation of Mr. Lukic in the kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I said, at the beginning in my statement to the investigators of the OTP, in so many words, I was an employee whose basic work was counter-intelligence and who was introduced into this case literally half an hour before the beginning of the interview with Milan Lukic. If you mean this first information, not the information I got from the interview with Milan Lukic, I had been with my colleague to attend talks that had been scheduled previously. I went there with my territorial colleague, the one who covers that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who was the source of the information regarding the alleged kidnapping and the involvement of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, as I said in the beginning, I didn't have an opportunity to speak with the witness prior to this, so I didn't an opportunity to advise him of courtroom procedures. But what I'd ask the Court to advise him is that if an answer to a question he believes implicates the security or the safety of someone, which is a question about confidential informants might, that he may raise that with the Chamber, and the Chamber may decide how best to deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, if you believe that any answer that you might give might affect the safety or security of a person, then you can bring that to our attention, because we have ways of dealing with that. Is there anything that you wish to say, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, I don't recall who the sources were. That interview was conducted by my colleague who covered that territory and who knows the sources in that territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so I ask you again: Isn't it true that a legal interrogation would have involved a full advice of rights including a formal waiver of rights to counsel being present during interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Obviously, he was not advised of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, again, it's fair to say that the conditions of an overnight interrogation are much more strenuous than a daytime interrogation allowing a suspect to have adequate rest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Obviously, they are more strenuous. The interview was conducted from 11.00 p.m. one day, until 9.00 a.m. the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Lukic was not charged with terrorism in relation to the crimes that you were investigating; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: My knowledge about further procedure with Mr. Lukic ended on the 28th after that interview. I conducted that interview with him from 11.00 p.m. until 9.00 a.m., and he was then turned over to the Secretariat of Internal Affairs of Uzice. Then according to a decision of the district prosecutor, he was remanded in custody for 48 hours. What happened with Mr. Lukic later, I don't know because that was not my job. My job was over, as far as he's concerned, when I drafted the official documents that have been shown here and when I reported to the competent unit above me. That's where my work with him ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true, though, that he was released two days later and those same weapons were released back to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I hear that from you for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, otherwise, isn't it true that you were only -- you only asked about and were interested in the Sjeverin incident which was on 22nd of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: My primary goal was to try to establish whether he was involved in that, and I tried and tried throughout the interview, where we went from topic to topic, but my primary focus was to try to establish whether he and his unit were involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But would it -- wouldn't it be fair to say, sir, that in intervening to arrest and detain Milan Lukic, your service was operating pursuant to some other authority, one beyond the scope and duties conferred upon the RDB by either the constitution of Serbia, the Law on Internal Affairs, or the rules of service of the RDB?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid is kindly asked to read more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my personal opinion, then and now, that Milan Lukic was arrested by accident at that border crossing. He was not arrested by the State Security Service. He was arrested by the police, from the police station in Priboj, that is, the public security sector, because they found weapons on him as well as forged IDs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, before you ask your next question, the interpreter is asking you to speak more slowly, particularly when you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And at this time, I'd like to ask the court assistant to approach the witness with a document to see if he recognises it and put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution would appreciate a copy, if there is one. This is a lengthy two-page document that I'm seeing for the first time. Is there a copy that I can have to look at while Mr. Alarid is working with the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We just received the documents, Your Honour, and had this one translated, the translation being held last night.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at this document for a moment. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I'm seeing it for the first time, I have to say that. But I see that it's a document from the district public prosecutor's office of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it's regarding formal charges or accusations regarding illegal use of weapons, correct -- or possession of weapons, rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I can't see it from this part of the document; it must be later in the statement of reasons. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would this be in conformity with the normal document issued by the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we show the witness the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please review this for a moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that, according to this document, Mr. Lukic was only held for the possession of weapons and identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you recognise the name of the deputy public prosecutor Mr. Ilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now can we go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'd like you to read the first sentence right underneath "Lukic and Dragicevic."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: You want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: "On 26 October 1992, around 1700 hours in Sjeverin, in a passenger vehicle, make Passat, licence plates GZ-585-22, they kept illegally," column, "two automatic rifles, factory numbers 108769 and 269422, manufactured by Crvena Zastava factory, with five clips of 30 rounds each; one automatic rifle," "Phoson," I suppose this word is, "factory number 91053, with two full clips (56 rounds) and one empty clip; four grenades (three M-75 grenades and one marks-72 grenade); one rifle launched grenade; one RPG grenade; one pistol poll made by Crvena Zastava of 7.65 millimetre caliber, factory number ..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's fine, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: -- "... which has been established by inspection conducted by members of the Special Police Unit of the SUP of Uzice who, thus, established that they had illegally obtained and kept firearms."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true, sir, that this document shows that Mr. Lukic was arrested on the 26th of October, not on the 27th; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Sir, the first time around when you asked me that question I was clear. Based on what I know, Milan Lukic was arrested on the 26th of October, probably sometime during that day. That evening, he was taken to Uzice, and this tallies with what we've just seen: The 26th of October, about 1700 hours in Sjeverin. So there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So would you defer to this document as proof of when and where Mr. Lukic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, is the witness able to do that? The fact that he defers doesn't establish that as a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I don't think that that is helpful at all. We will have to make up our minds about the document. Please ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, sir, would it otherwise be true that you don't, in fact, know the exact time and place of Mr. Lukic's arrest because you weren't there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: That's true, I wasn't there. That much is certain. I was informed that he had been arrested in the Serbia's territory, which at the time seemed to be the border crossing, and was subsequently taken to Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How far is Sjeverin from where you said he was originally arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true it's 15 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I assume that this might be the case, 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's because you've been there at least once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, I've never been there, not even once.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A moment to confer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would tender the demand of the public prosecutor against Milan Lukic, dated the 30th of October, 1992, for identification and -- but we would still, of course, need to uploaded and place the evidence into the electronic database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Exactly what document is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's the official -- it's the document that was on the ELMO, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you want it marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, actually, we'd like to tender the exhibit and introduce the exhibit, Your Honour; but we, of course, haven't gone through the process of getting it uploaded and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, on its face, some terrible things were said about me when I disclosed documents late. I received this just while the witness is on the stand. Just looking at it, it seems, to me, on its face, illogical. If counsel took the position which the Chamber agreed that this man was unable to authenticate a document produced by his organisation, that he can somehow authenticate a document by some other organisation. But having said, Your Honour, when I read the document, it seems that much of it is corroborated by the other evidence we have heard from this witness. So, in this particular case, I will not object to the admission of this document, but that's not to sacrifice any other rights we would have in the future with respect to other late disclosures of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1D62.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true, sir, that Mr. Milan Lukic was on assignment from the military at the time of his arrest, his military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Is that a question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it's a question to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Based on what he told me during the interview, yes, he was on a military mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, in fact, he was released and acquitted of the charges later on, or at least released from the charges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: During the relevant time period of Mr. Lukic's arrest and questioning by your service, who was the top man of the RDB? Who was chief of the sector?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We can go into private session, Your Honour, if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only invoke facts that I received a waiver in relation to for the purposes of my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Frenki Simatovic was one of the persons highly placed within your service during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: This is the first time you ask me the question; but now that you've asked, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that RDB personnel, known as Frenki's boys, were on the ground in Bosnian and engaged in fighting, including Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you please tell us your knowledge of the crimes alleged against Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I have no knowledge at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But it would seem to me that what you were investigating Mr. Lukic in the same area and sector was -- is of a similar nature of the crimes alleged against Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I think that, of all things, goes to prove the fact that I didn't know at the time. The substance of the document tallies in its entirety with what I was told by Milan Lukic during the actual interview, and that is why I recorded this in writing in a literal way. It wasn't my place to assess the reliability of what Milan Lukic was telling me. My task was to establish any evidence that may have existed at the time of his potential involvement in the kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that these bosses of yours within the RDB are alleged to have been part of a joint criminal enterprise involving, amongst others, Milosevic and the Serbian political and military and police organs in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the relevance of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It goes to bias and motive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Elaborate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I mean, this witness comes in under what I think are unusual protective measures for police officers. Where I come from, police officers testify completely open and obvious because that is the badge that they represent. So, in this particular case, the country of Serbia has requested what I think are extreme protective measures, especially given the scope of what this witness was going to testify to. It is on that basis that I follow this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I still don't follow how the question that you asked about the joint criminal enterprise involving Milosevic and others can raise a question of bias.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, only because, Your Honours, the OTP has injected this -- this spectre of these October kidnappings into the case. I mean, we've already kind of fought that fight in terms of the relevance and applicability in relation to an alibi rebuttal; but since it's out here, that is for that reasoning that I'm following this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're not satisfied that it is relevant, Mr. Alarid, so please move on to another topic. I believe we have to stop now though for the break. We will break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, as part of the detention and booking process, did you or any of your colleagues record the physical appearance of Mr. Lukic as well as recording his personal details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It was in the ICTY field office in Belgrade that I provided my recollection of how I saw Milan Lukic after he had arrived there for the interview.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could all the other microphones please be switched off while the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, would it be fair to say that it would be standard procedure to record a suspect's full physical appearance as part of an investigator's note?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, it is the standard procedure, but this man was handcuffed when he was brought in wearing a uniform. At one point during the interview, I offered him a meal, since this was a lengthy interview, which he refused. It was not like he was drained or exhausted or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I'm asking the basics: Height, weight, age, hair colour, eye colour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Those details were not taken during my interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And wouldn't that be standard procedure to take those kind of details as part of a criminal investigation of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I assume so. But, again, I'm telling you he was taken into custody and detained by the Uzice SUP -- rather, the Priboj police station, and this was Priboj territory. All the details were taken by the employees of the Uzice SUP. That is why I'm telling you this. Once he arrived in my office, everyone knew that this person was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What did you do to verify this information, because, of course, this person was arrested with false identification.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: What did I do to verify this information? I spoke to him. He said he was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why would you trust the simple affirmation of a person that was caught with fake identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, I had every confidence that the Uzice SUP people had done their job properly when they ID'd him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, one thing is that these -- this false identification was actually issued by the Visegrad police department. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have any time or contact with the relevant police authorities in Visegrad for information collection or collaboration of the identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why not? It seems like it would be important to call Visegrad and ask them regarding this identification.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, establishing his identity and establishing the fact that these were forged documents, these were two things that were the responsibility of the Uzice SUP. It was after all of that, that Milan Lukic was brought to my office, to my institution. I was then told that he had been found in possession of a false ID bearing the name that was stated in the Official Note. It was also pointed out to me that this person I was now facing was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Prosecutor used one hour and ten minutes; and to have equal time, you have another 18 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, if need be, Your Honour, I would ask my co-counsel for some of their time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let's just see how we get ahead, let us see how we get ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know Risto Perisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Heard of, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have personal ties with Perisic or professional ties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No ties at all. The name rings familiar, and I think I actually saw the man on occasion, but I certainly have no ties to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that he was the commander of the police in Visegrad at that time and a high-ranking member of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I can't say that he wasn't, but I only heard of Risto Perisic at a later stage, not back then. Visegrad was, to me, a secret all the way. I didn't exactly know who was who in Visegrad, and it certainly wasn't part of my job to investigate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why do you use the word "secret"? Why was Visegrad a secret all the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Risto Perisic, I didn't mean Risto Perisic as such. Visegrad as a town was not in my field of vision then. It was not an object of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you used the term Visegrad was a secret to you, and I want to know what you meant by the term "secret."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: When I said "secret," I meant that at that time I had absolutely no idea what was going on in Visegrad, who was in which position. It's a place close to Uzice, and many people came to Uzice from Visegrad for various reasons, fleeing or otherwise, seeking shelter, seeking safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it -- isn't it correct that following the removal of Stanisic by Milosevic, the Serbian State Security Service did everything but their job including the involvement of the assassination of the Democratic prime minister and attempted assassination of the Democratic opposition leader, Draskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I didn't get that. Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that following the removal of Stanisic by Slobodan Milosevic, the Serbian State Security Service was involved in the assassination of the Democratic prime minister and the attempted assassination of the Democratic opposition leader, Vuk Draskovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the relevance of that, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- it's part of our defence that, in some ways, Mr. Lukic is a scapegoat on certain issues that he's accused with, including this kidnapping. We are trying to establish the inter-relationship between the governments of Serbia and Bosnia, the -- the cooperation and collaboration, if you will, of this otherwise large-scale war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I haven't ruled on it. All right. Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question seems very out of place to me. I don't see what kind of answer I would be able to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You can answer with what you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I can tell you that I worked as an employee of that service, and I can tell you that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- worked with full --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Alarid -- Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a general objection. Mr. Alarid is taking a rather rigid position with respect to witnesses that have been called for alibi, and has held me to task any time he feels that I've ventured outside these parameters. Is it his view now that on cross-examination witnesses caught for alibi that other areas of interest of the defence may be explored with them? If that's the case, then I would ask for the same -- the same flexibility when asking questions of witnesses that have been called strictly for alibi.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I mean, under the Rules, Your Honour, we are contesting the credibility of the witness, and I think that goes beyond the normal scope of alibi, and I think the door was opened since considering the Prosecution's presentation of this witness greatly exceeded the normal alibi rebuttal scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you at any time during your investigation verify whether or not Milan Lukic was a member of the Visegrad police force or reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, I did not check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did any part of your investigation reveal involvement of the Visegrad police in any of the events related to the allegations against Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I can repeat verbatim the Official Note that I made. It reflects all my knowledge at the time, and I stand behind it. Not even at the time when I was writing the document, having talked to Mr. Lukic, at no point did I evaluate the validity of whatever he told me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mikes off, thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- verbatim what he said during that interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where can we find your investigative file from your service relating to this crime charged against Milan Lukic, including the results of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: That's something you have to ask the current service or the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because would it be fair to say that your investigative note would just be part -- become part of a larger file that was regarding the entire investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I can tell you with full responsibility. My interview with Milan Lukic was the initial interview with him, it was conducted on the premises of our service, and I informed the leadership of the service about the interview. I had no further assignments in this connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be customary for the entire written file to be kept by the RDB or the security service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I suppose so. It's possible that it's somewhere in the documentation of the service, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, would it be true that scouts in the military or on military assignments were given false documentation if they were to go behind enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: At that time, it was said that people who were going to that area of Bosnia were changing names. They didn't need an identity. I don't know. I mentioned that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question was, more specifically: Was it not uncommon for false identities to be given to scouts behind enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is not part of the military. Does he have a basis of knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If he can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly it. I don't know. I've never have any contact with the military and their services.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how long were you employed by the State Security Service of Serbia in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: In the service of the state security sector of Serbia, a little short of 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And as part of your ongoing presence for the state security sector, did you ever have any information that Mr. Lukic was an employee of the Serbian police force, the Serbian MUP, in any capacity, at any time before, during, or after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I never had such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever have information that Milan Lukic was a source of the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Has it ever been presented to you information of whether or not Milan Lukic was a cadet or finished the Serbian police academy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to where Milan Lukic lived and was registered prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Apart from the information that Milan Lukic himself provided during the interview, I had absolutely no other information about Milan Lukic; and let me repeat again. I did not evaluate the information he provided. What was important to me and what I focused on was to note down exactly what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, again, this was strictly related to the allegations of October 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you verify Mr. Lukic's apartment in Belgrade for simple background verification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Let me tell you, my engagement concerning Milan Lukic ended on the 28th October 1992. My job was very limited: To conduct that interview in that room and to go out into the field were my colleague the next day. I had no contact with Milan Lukic before or after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that you were able to verify that Milan Lukic had a registration and licence for a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: It was not my job at all to establish whether he had a licence to carry two automatic rifles, grenades, et cetera, in the territory of Serbia. He was found carrying them. And according to the laws applying then, he had violated our laws, and because of that he was taken into custody in Uzice and then brought to me in the office of the service, where I conducted my interview with him. So we used this room given to us to conduct an interview with him and question him about the circumstances of crimes we were interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, being interested in the kidnapping at Sjeverin, isn't it true that there was only a single source for the allegations of Milan Lukic in that case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Let me tell you, at that time, as I understood it, because I had been briefed about Milan Lukic half an hour [as interpreted] before the interview, I was briefed by both the public security and the state security sector, and my Official Note reflects only the information that I obtained from talking to him. There's nothing else in that note. Whatever else is written is the result of my talks with my other colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just a correction for the transcript, Mr. Ivetic states that he -- that the witness stated that he had been briefed about Milan Lukic "an hour" before the interview, not "half an hour," at page 84, line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So, sir, you mean to tell me that, as part of your briefing, you weren't given the general source and information regarding the allegations against Milan Lukic? You weren't given a background that would allow you to answer -- or ask questions in a logical manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: In that briefing, I was told that there was indicia, there is information indicating that Milan Lukic and his group had been involved in those kidnappings. The talk with Milan Lukic started with the general background allowing us to come to that issue. Milan Lukic strenuously denied his involvement in that crime during the interview, and my job was to continue talking to him and lead him back to that topic. As you can see from the note that I made reflecting the interview with Milan Lukic, he denies most strenuously that he had been involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What information did you possess indicating that Mr. Lukic and his group had been involved? That's the point I'm trying to get to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: What information? All I can tell you is based on my recollection. It was information that he was arrested precisely in that area, which is close to the site of the incident of the kidnapping. Based on the knowledge available then, we were not able to say definitively that Milan Lukic was involved. The kidnappings took place on the 22nd, and the interview was on the 26th. We had no confirmation, no solid information that he was involved. That's what the interview was about, where he was moving around, where he was travelling, what he had been doing before, so that we were able to put together the picture, the puzzle, and I think that's reflected in the Official Note which you have in your possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But what I want to know is: What information did you have, no matter how sketchy or inconclusive it was? What was the source of your information, and what information did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, you know, I'm telling you again. I was briefed for that interview an hour before. I was told what the service knew about him and about the whole case and what the clues and indicia were. My colleague, the territorial colleague who was much better informed, was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But what I want to know is what you were informed. All the indicia that you just mentioned during that briefing, you have not yet commented on. Please tell us, what information did you have during that briefing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: In the course of the briefing, I was told that indicia existed indicating that Milan Lukic, leader of the Avengers group, had participated in the kidnappings of the citizens from Sjeverin, and that was the entire basis on which I had to conduct the interview. There was this allegation, and I didn't put it to him by saying, "You were involved." I asked, "Were you involved?" His answers were negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, again, I ask you: What indicia did you have? What knowledge was in your brain from any other sources or any place that he had, in fact, been involved? This didn't come out of thin air.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I keep telling you, all the information I had is what I mentioned. That's all I could use in the interview. If I had more conclusive evidence or indicia, the whole interview would have been conducted in a completely different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that your source regarding the indicia that we're having such a hard time getting to indicated that the Sjeverin kidnappees were in front of the Visegrad police station in a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, no, no. Absolutely not. I don't know, in fact. That information that those people were in the truck was something I learnt a day after my interview with Milan Lukic. At the time of the interview, I didn't know that. I didn't even try to find the source of the indicia. I had only a limited time to prepare for that interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, so, you didn't have a knowledge of -- of an informant or source reporting seeing the truck with 15 to 16 persons parked outside the Visegrad SUP on the 22nd of October at 7.45 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: In the course of the interview with Milan Lukic, when it started, I had no idea about that. That interview with Milan Lukic was on the 26th from 11.00 p.m. on the 26th, then it ended the next morning at 7.00 a.m. The conversation with that other source took place on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have now used ten minutes in excess of the time used by the Prosecutor, which was an hour and ten minutes, and I'll give you at maximum another ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I have in my hand here, and this was the document that the Prosecution was having a hard time getting on the screen, but it's from that document that comes the information regarding the truck in front of the SUP and Visegrad with the persons. So I'm not sure how we can get him to identify it and go to there, but it might take a little more time than the ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us work with ten minutes in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that a report issued on the 2nd of November, 1992, references the truck that we're talking about and the persons at the Visegrad SUP? It's a report by the RDB of Uzice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes. So one thing is the report concerning the interview with Milan Lukic, and another thing is the report concerning interviews with two other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And are these the sources that you -- are these the sources that you can name now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, to clarify, that was not the document that I was trying to put up on the ELMO. I believe -- I'm not sure which documents Mr. Alarid is referring to, but it may be the subject of a very recent application by the government of Serbia for protective measures. So that we don't deny them the opportunity for a decision on that, could I ask that a discussion of this document be held in closed session? At least that way we preserve the confidentiality of the matter until the government of Serbia has been fully heard on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But the question specifically, sir, was: Were you aware of a journalist that had documented the condition of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Based on what I heard from the sources that I talked to, that would have seemed -- that would have seemed to be the case, and this is clearly stated in my note. There was circumstantial evidence to the effect that such-and-such a journalist had taken such-and-such photographs. It is in the Official Note, and I believe you are actually in possession of those documents, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you aware that that journalist was arrested in Belgrade and the photographs confiscated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If they -- if this journalist had been arrested, would it have been by the same organisation that employed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, it's not my place to draw conclusions. My task was over the day I finished those documents; and, again, as far as Milan Lukic was concerned, I never had anything at all to do with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that nothing about your investigation questioned Mr. Lukic about June 7th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: The 7th of June, what is that supposed to be in relation to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So that's a no; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I have no idea what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that nothing about your investigation questioned Mr. Lukic about June 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: These dates don't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that your investigation did not question Mr. Lukic about June 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I certainly don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, one more question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know one thing, sir, you're asking me about dates, dates that were 16 years ago, and you're not even indicating what may have happened on those dates. I'm unable to answer unless this is something from one of my documents, and that might be helpful in terms of jogging my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just one more question that the Court has allowed me: Isn't it true that your investigation didn't question him about June 27th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: I don't know what that date is in relation to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a few brief questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-142, on page 71, beginning at line 25 of the transcript, you were asked the following question by Mr. Alarid: "And isn't it true, sir, that Milan Lukic was on assignment from the military at the time of his arrest, his military?" And you responded: "Based on what he told me during the interview, yes, he was on a military mission." Were you aware of any military operations that were being conducted by persons from Visegrad on the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, calls for speculation, especially since on direct exam and cross-exam, the witness denied knowledge of the military operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. But it's a simple question, whether he had any knowledge of the military operations. What is your answer, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the area included in the document that I produced, and all I know about military operations in the area is what Milan Lukic told me. You keep mixing up two different notions that are to be kept apart. As far as I know, Milan Lukic was arrested in the territory of Serbia. This is something that is mentioned in the municipal prosecutor's documents, the location being specified as Sjeverin. I suppose you have a map, so you can check the location of this village. That was what he told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next question I have for you is that you testified - I'm referring to the transcript at the top of page 76 - you offered him some food, a meal. Did you also offer him something to drink over the course of this lengthy interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes, water. The interview took a long time. I said the man should be given something to eat or drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, my last question to you is that Mr. Alarid has suggested to you that your department had no legitimate reason to question Milan Lukic with respect to what was going on or about these hostages that had been seized from Sjeverin. So I put the question to you: In your view were you engaged in an interview that was within the confines of your legal jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for a legal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You could put it more simply, Mr. Groome --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- by asking him what, in his view, was the basis for the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to address the question posed Judge Robinson: What, in your view, was the basis of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Our investigation at that point was to simply try and talk to Milan Lukic, to ascertain, if possible, whether he had been present in the area at the indicated time in which the kidnapping of citizens of Sjeverin took place. He said he was on a military mission in the area, and we tried to put two and two together, in a manner of speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when did you interviewed him, did you believe you were acting within your authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-142
utterances.text: Yes. I believed that I was in the strictest compliance, in fact, with the rules of my work during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, this is the end of your testimony here, but we have been informed that there is a matter that you might wish to raise with us concerning your status as a witness. If you wish to do that, then you may do so now; otherwise, you are perfectly free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, you don't have to stand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. I came to the Belgrade office of the International Tribunal because of a summons that I had been served by the District Court in Belgrade, and this came through my work, my office. I went there of my own free will and in keeping with the law on cooperation with the ICTY. I went there to talk about documents that I produced back in 1992. The documents were produced for the purposes of the service of which I was an employee. There was just one thing that I asked both the office and the Prosecutor and the Tribunal itself, this being for me to be called as a Chamber's witness, not a Defence or OTP witness, the Court's witness. I have been misled in a way because when I came here, I was informed that I would be appearing here as an OTP witness, but at least the evidence I gave was solely about my authorship of these documents and the circumstances surrounding the Milan Lukic interview. That is all I wish to say about this matter, Your Honours. These documents were produced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand, then, that you would have preferred to have been a witness for the Court, a Chamber witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to express my objection to any kind of re-characterisation of the witness. He was called as a witness using my legal authority as a member of the Office of the Prosecutor. When he declined to come voluntarily, again, under the law, I made an application to the Chamber and the Chamber issued a subpoena. There's been nothing that the Office of the Prosecutor has done to act in any way inappropriate with this witness, and I'm sure if it's explained to Mr. VG-142 that just as he conducted himself within the confines of the law in questioning the people he questioned, that it was within my authority to call him as a witness. I know there are some misperceptions about the Office of the Prosecutor down in Serbia, but I don't think at that we should give them any substance which re-characterising what, in fact, happened in this case, and that is that the Prosecution called him as a witness. When he declined to speak with me yesterday, I honoured his wish and only addressed him here in the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, we understand what you have said. You've just heard what the Prosecutor himself said. The jurisprudence of the Tribunal is that there is no property in a witness, and so we are very grateful to you for coming. Had we been advised in specific terms before that you desired to be a Chamber witness, then we would have ruled on that question, but we thank you very much for the evidence that you have given, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. But if you look at paragraph 1 of my statement in the ICTY field office, this was precisely what I said. I think you had to know because that was the first thing I said. I said I volunteer to appear, but I do have one express desire. I want to be a witness of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your mic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session for a decision that I have to give.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of October, 2008, at 8.50 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
